history.summary: Freehold D15 3BR (1,528sqft) at $2.0M / $1,309psf, 470m to Kembangan MRT — looks cheap, but Radix is a 21-unit boutique with only 4 URA transactions and 3.2% yield. The headline MMR 807 is an artifact of thin data; illiquidity is the real story.
history.rating_rationale: On paper attractive: freehold, large 1,528sqft, $1,309psf well under the (thin) $1,445 median, 470m to Kembangan EW6, desirable D15. But the development has just 21 units total and only 4 URA transactions — the 7.49%/yr CAGR and MMR 807 / score 807 are statistically meaningless and must be heavily discounted (anti-anchoring). A 21-unit block means shallow exit liquidity: any single forced seller moves the market, and price discovery is poor. Reviews note exclusivity/privacy as a plus but that is an own-stay virtue, not an investment one. Freehold + large size + location give real downside support, so not an Avoid — but thin liquidity and unreliable appreciation data cap it firmly at Neutral.
red_flags: Only 21 units — extremely shallow liquidity, poor price discovery on exit
Just 4 URA transactions — appreciation rate (7.49%) and MMR 807 unreliable, ignore
3.2% gross yield is mediocre for the price; boutique blocks lack facilities/scale
catalysts: Freehold tenure — no lease decay, long-term hold safety
470m / 6-min walk to Kembangan MRT in deep-buyer-pool D15
Large 1,528sqft at $1,309psf — low absolute PSF gives downside cushion
